item.title: Ask HN: Is there a stronger moat in marketplaces in the age of SaaS AI Slop?
item.summary: Basically, what I’m trying to say is: software is cheap to produce now, but not necessarily easy to customize. It seems like everyone is honing in on distribution and capital as the moat. We have all these vibe-coding platforms and a flood of applications that are 90% there but not quite finished. Then everyone is trying to get that last 10% and capture the value there. The people winning so far are mostly agencies, right? Or hackers going door to door and selling custom solutions. But what’s killing them is the shenanigans around customer acquisition, growth hacking and stuff like that. I think startups promising things like 'your agentic CMO in a box' are a symptom of this, and personally not yet fully convinced on their utility, as much respect as I have for many cracked founders selling shovels. I don’t know if anyone saw Outbid.lol, the pay-to-rank leaderboard that just went viral on X and immediately spawned a brigade of copycats, but it made me really think: are marketplaces going to actually be more defensible now than pure software? Because if code is abundant, then yeah, the moat has moved to the distribution side. But maybe the other moat is making software really, reall
